messages.author: d1a447e1c9bca559
messages.subject: cov.unscaled in summary.lm
parts:
Shalom,
In the help function of summary.lm it says that cov.unscaled is:
a p x p matrix of (unscaled) covariances of the coef[j], j=1, …, p.

What does it mean unscaled?

The simple covariance of the coefficients is given by the function vcov()

Thank you
Ronen

messages.author: c7a0d087ca7b2eb2
messages.subject: Re: cov.unscaled in summary.lm
parts:
when running summary.lm(object,correlation=F) there is the switch for correlation matrix, which is the scaled covariance matrix. the function calulates the covariance matrix by default and if correlation=T then it adds the scaled correlation matrix to the result arguments of the function.

if you want to see exact calculations run
